In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AtHMA4 is not involved in Zn tolerance but in Zn sensitivity in tobacco.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AtHMA4 overexpression in tobacco results in enhanced Zn accumulation in the root and leaf tissues.

AtHMA4 is involved in the control of Zn translocation to the shoot, and the expression of this gene in tobacco leads to an enhanced Zn sensitivity phenotype due to the overloading of the root and leaf cell walls with Zn.
the expression of AtHMA4 results in a shift in the balance of the Zn homeostasis network in tobacco, which is reflected in a higher sensitivity to Zn.
The main takeaway from our work is that

AtHMA4 is an important determinant of apoplastic Zn homeostasis in tobacco, and this can be used to manipulate Zn homeostasis for the improvement of crop yield under conditions of Zn deficiency and Zn toxicity.
AtHMA4 can contribute to Zn tolerance in tobacco, and that this tolerance is dependent on the apoplast Zn levels.
Zn sensitivity of AtHMA4 expressing plants is not caused by the accumulation of Zn in the vacuole or the cytoplasm, but by the increased loading of the leaf and root apoplast.
